steps.text: The axis of symmetry of y = ax² + bx + c is x = −b/(2a).
Here a = 1 and b = 2.
Simplify.
The answer is option b).
The vertex lies on the axis of symmetry: x = −b/(2a).
Substitute x = −1 into f to find the y-coordinate.
Simplify.
The vertex is (−1, −4): option c).
The y-intercept is the value of f when x = 0.
Simplify.
The graph crosses the y-axis at (0, −3): option b).
Use x = −b/(2a) with a = −1 and b = 8.
Simplify.
The axis of symmetry is the vertical line x = 4: option a).
Find the turning point (lowest point) of the parabola on the grid.
Read its coordinates: it lies 2 units left of the y-axis and 3 units below the x-axis.
The vertex is (−2, −3): option B).
The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through the vertex.
The vertex of the parabola is at x = 1 on the grid.
The axis of symmetry is x = 1: option A).
The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis (x = 0).
Read the y-value at the crossing point on the grid.
The y-intercept is y = 4: option C).
